## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0a7ff7ca7c078872d221ddd87df185f0db04248f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md + none
Security-touching: yes

This record answers the contract-review claim posted on the PR as comment 7154525435. Inputs: card #37202 with every comment, PR #37240 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Cited code was read on `origin/main` at `ad604c10`; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is one file, `docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md`, 31 lines added and 11 removed. It publishes nothing: no schema, no code, no generated output. Right.
- The `Status:` line is unchanged, so the generated `docs/adr/README.md` is rightly absent from the diff. The check-runs agree (`Lint · docs & code guards` success).
- The accept-set the text declares for row 11 is new: three optional keys on a `related` entry. On `main` `AiContextRelatedSchema` is strict and refuses all three, as the text says. Declaring them here and landing them with their reader is the ADR-0049 order. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: every run concluded success or skipped; none failed, none is pending.

Citations, each read on `origin/main`:

- `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts#FilterConditionSchema` exists. The ten admitted operators are all members of `FILTER_OPERATORS`; `$between`, the five string operators and `$empty` are the rest of that list, and `LOGICAL_OPERATORS` is `$and`, `$or`, `$not`. `FieldOperatorsSchema` also carries `$like` and `$ilike`, which neither list holds; the text's "anything else is refused" covers them. True.
- `packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts#SortNodeSchema` is `{ field, order }`, strict, with `aliases: { direction: 'order' }`. It refuses `direction` by name. True. Its `order` defaults to `asc`.
- `RECORD_CONTEXT_RELATED_MAX_ROWS` is 20 in `record-context-tools.ts` and is pinned by test. True.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-relation-reads.ts#RelatedListRequest` carries `orderBy` and `limit` and no `where`. `get_record`'s input schema (`mcp-http-tools.ts`) bounds `limit` with `.max(relatedMaxRows)`, so a limit over its cap is refused at parse. True. That cap is the lower of 20 and the door's own page cap.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts#assertReadableQueryFields` refuses a query whose `where` or `orderBy` names a field marked `readable: false` in the map it is handed. The map is one field-level derivation, so a field the caller's schema hides and a field the schema shows while field-level security withholds it are refused alike. True as far as the text goes; see S1 for what the text leaves out.

### ② Semver level

No changeset, and the PR carries `skip-changeset`. That matches: an ADR amendment publishes no package. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right for this PR; row 11 makes its own declaration (`added`), as the split table says.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's three open questions:

- (a) A `limit` over the cap: refused at parse, or cut? Refused at parse is right, as written. The record already says a pack over a bound is refused at parse and nothing is cut silently at call time, and `get_record` refuses the same key the same way. The cost is real and the text names it: the spec schema cannot import the service's constant, so row 11 must declare one number both read.
- (b) Bare-value equality is not admitted. The plain reading does refuse it, and the text does not say so. That is part of S2.
- (c) Does "cannot read" cover both the schema-hidden and the withheld field? Yes, and it must: the narrower rule of card #37203 would leave the withheld case to a whole-call 403. But two cases are still one short. See S1.

The four out-of-scope findings in the dev report are carried, not answered here. Two matter to row 11: the service on `main` refuses the whole call for a child this caller is not served, and a link field that field-level security withholds reaches the predicate guard. Both predate this diff.

SQL push-down: the text keeps the child read as one query, with the filter, the order and the cut inside it. No id materialisation and no in-app join is added.

The card's acceptance says the PR stays draft. The PR reads `draft: false` at this head. That is the seat's to settle, not a finding on the text.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the first consumer (row 5 on `main`: `ai-context.zod.ts` and `service-record-context`) and the execution plan (row 11, card #37203).

**S1 (should-fix) — "cannot read" misses the field the caller reads masked.** D3 drops the section when `where` or `orderBy` names a field "this caller cannot read", in two cases: hidden by the schema, or shown and withheld. The guard the text cites refuses a third. Its call site hands it `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms`, which also marks as non-queryable a field this caller sees partially masked, and a field readable only under the agent ceiling. The spec says the same: `ISecurityService.getQueryableFields` is "a subset of `getReadableFields`", and "the difference between the two is exactly the fields this caller sees masked". D3 also says a masked value is carried as served, so such a caller can read the field in the record's own sense. Row 11, built to the text, would send that caller's query, and the engine would answer 403 for the whole call. That breaks "a field-level rule never refuses a pack". The text's own reason ("rows chosen or ordered by a value disclose it") applies to a masked value in full. The fail direction is closed, so this is not a leak. The fix is one sentence: the rule is "a field this caller cannot query on", the complement of `getQueryableFields`, and the header bullet and card #37203's item 3 follow.

**S2 (should-fix) — the comparand side of `where` is not closed in words.** The text closes the operator side and says "anything else is refused at parse". Two comparand forms are left to row 11 to guess:

- The bare value. `FilterConditionSchema`'s first form is implicit equality, `{ is_current: true }`. The plain reading refuses it; the dev's own recommendation is to admit it. The record must say one or the other, because row 11's parser and its refusal message depend on it.
- The placeholder string. The engine resolves a comparand that is entirely `{token}` in every `where` it reads (`resolveFilterTokens`, called from the engine's find path): `{today}`, `{now}`, `{30_days_ago}`, `{current_user_id}`, `{current_org_id}`. Such a string is a literal to the parser, so it passes the ten operators. The text refuses the `$now` anchor and is silent on `{now}`. With these, a pack's selection depends on the clock and on the caller. And a token the engine does not know, or `{record_id}`, throws at call time for every caller: an author defect that is neither refused at parse nor listed among the author defects.

Neither changes the read set or grants anything. Both are contract shape, so the record should settle them: admit or refuse the bare value, and admit a named token list or refuse the whole-`{…}` string at parse.

**S3 (should-fix) — the record's account of where its text comes from is wrong.** The header says the amendment is by the maintainer's word and that "one sentence does not come from that word". The PR body lists ten more places that go past it. After the merge the PR body is gone and the record stands alone. The record has a section for exactly this, "Points that go past the card's words", which says which settlements are the record's own and which needed the maintainer. The amendment updates point 5 only. Point 11, the hidden structural field, is not updated for `where` and `orderBy`, though D3 now adds them. The settlements that change what an author or a user sees belong there by name: the operator set, the parse refusal of a `limit` over the cap, the section dropped for a field the caller cannot query, and the bare-value answer of S2. None of the eleven is the maintainer's own decision in the maintainer's words; each is the record's settlement, accepted by the merge. The text should say that, and the header's "one sentence" should not imply the rest was dictated.

Do the eleven places stay within the maintainer's word? They stay within its subject. Each narrows or spells out filter and order on `related`; none adds reach. Places 1, 2, 8, 9 and 10 are readings of the tree and are true. Places 3, 4, 6 and 7 follow rules the record already has. Place 5 is S1. Place 11 is true: PR #37222 has merged, and `main` holds `RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES` (80), pinned by test, with a stated cut (`outlineTruncated`).

Does "the read set is unchanged" hold? Yes. `where` and `orderBy` name the child's own fields, the nested relation condition and the dotted key are refused, and `limit` is a number. The read-set function on `main` (`read-set.ts`) reads the root, each `related[].object` and the lookup targets, and takes nothing from the three keys. A placeholder token reads no object either.

Nits, none of which changes the contract:

- Nit: `limit` itself is a twelfth place past the verbatim word, which names filter and order. The card names it and the PR's summary for the maintainer says it, so the merge covers it. The numbered list should carry it.
- Nit: "the data engine refuses" the filter. The refusal is the security plugin's engine middleware. A deployment without that plugin has no such guard.
- Nit: an outline is also cut by the body's character bound, before it reaches the entry cap. The new sentence names the entry cap alone.
- Nit: `where` has no bound on its size (conditions, nesting, `$in` members), while the record bounds every other part of a pack at parse. Row 11 can set one.
- Nit: `get_record`'s cap is the lower of 20 and the door's page cap. On a door with a lower page cap, a `limit` that parsed is lowered at call time. Row 11 must state that cut.
- Nit: the link-field sentence next to the new one still says "that caller's schema hides". The new sentence is wider, so the two now differ in one bullet. A follow-up card should carry it.

The call site builds its map with `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms` (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`), which also refuses a field the caller reads masked and an agent-ceiling field; the spec's `getQueryableFields` says the same. If row 11 is built to the text as written, such a caller gets a whole-call 403, against D3's "a field-level rule never refuses a pack". Fix: say "a field this caller cannot query on" (the complement of `getQueryableFields`), in D3 and in the Amended summary.
- **L2 S2. The comparand side of `where` is not closed in words.**
  - Bare-value equality is left undecided; this is the dev's open point (b).
  - Whole-`{token}` placeholder strings (`{today}`, `{now}`, `{current_user_id}`) pass the filter parser and the engine resolves them, while the text refuses only the `$now` anchor.
  - An unknown token or `{record_id}` fails every caller's call at run time, and the author-defect paragraph does not list it.

  - the record's own "Points that go past the card's words" section is not extended;
  - its point 11 is not updated for `where` and `orderBy`.
  
  Fix: list the places in that section, or at least the ones that change what row 11 builds, and correct the header sentence. `limit` itself is a twelfth place past the verbatim 「筛选和排序」 (L2 nit).

### The dev's three open points

- **(a)** A `limit` over the cap refused at parse: right, as the pack's other bounds are, and as `get_record` refuses an over-cap `limit`.
- **(b)** Bare-value equality: the plain reading refuses it, but the text must say so (S2).
- **(c)** "Cannot read" covering both schema-hidden and FLS-withheld fields: right, and still one case short (S1).

### Read and found right (head 0a7ff7ca)

- **`l1-face --pr 37240`.**
  - The face reads base `main`, `Fixes #37202` binding only this card, and `skip-changeset` right (no published package is touched).
  - Declarations: `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is right for a record that declares and implements nothing. Row 11 declares `added`.
  - At my read, 18 success, 0 failed and 5 pending; the L2's later read found all success or skipped.
- **`Fixes` is right, once the findings close.** Card #37202's What list is all in the diff:
  - D1 `where` / `orderBy` / `limit`, and their removal from Later work;
  - D3 "runs inside the caller's one capped query, grants nothing", and the hidden-field drop;
  - D4 "read set unchanged";
  - point 5;
  - row 11;
  - the Amended line quoting 「related 的筛选和排序 同意」.
  
  The row-11 card it names, #37203, exists and is the implementation card.
- **Citations.** The L2 confirmed every one on `origin/main`:
  - the ten operators in `FILTER_OPERATORS`;
  - `SortNodeSchema` strict `{ field, order }`, refusing `direction`;
  - `RECORD_CONTEXT_RELATED_MAX_ROWS` = 20;
  - `RelatedListRequest` taking `orderBy` and `limit`, with no `where` and an over-cap `.max`;
  - `assertReadableQueryFields`.
  
  The carried N5 sentence is true: #37222 has merged, with `RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES` = 80 and a stated cut.

### For the seat

This PR left draft at 06:11Z (`ready_for_review` by os-zhuang), and the card's acceptance says it "stays draft with `pm:awaiting-merge` until the maintainer merges it". A person did it, so this is a note for the seat, not a finding on the text. Nothing here arms or queues it.

2. L1-w: a new claim, the same L2 reviewer reads the delta, and I read the L1 delta.
3. Then the seat hands it to the maintainer.

This is the delta record for the head above. It answers the contract-review claim posted on the PR as comment 7155328202, and follows the round-1 record, comment 7154648352, which left S1, S2 and S3 open. The delta is a merge of `main` and one text commit. Inputs: card #37202 with every comment, PR #37240 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the delta between the two heads, and the check-runs on this head. Cited code was read on `main` at `6211ddf4`; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- The net diff against `main` is still one file, `docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md`, now 55 lines added and 13 removed. It publishes nothing. Right.
- The `Status:` line is unchanged, so the generated `docs/adr/README.md` is rightly absent.
- The merge of `main` brought the cross-reference note of objectstack#37180 into the file. It is `main`'s text, not this PR's, and is outside the net diff.
- Check-runs on this head: 26 success, 22 skipped, none failed, none pending.

Citations the delta adds, each read on `main` at `6211ddf4`:

- `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts#getQueryableFields` exists. Its contract says the answer is the exact complement of what the engine's predicate guard refuses, a subset of `getReadableFields`, and that the difference is the fields this caller sees masked. It also says a consumer with no answer treats every field with a masking rule as not queryable. The text's sentences match.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts#computeQueryGuardFieldPerms` exists. It folds in the field-permission map, the delegator's map by intersection, the partial-mask rules and the computed fields that read a withheld field. Each of the five cases D3 now lists is in it. True.
- `packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts#FILTER_TOKEN_WRAPPED_RE` is `^\$?\{([^{}]+)\}$`: one whole token, with or without a leading `$`. True.
- `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts#resolveFilterTokens` resolves every string comparand, list members included, through the spec's classifier, which uses that same pattern. An unknown token throws, and `{record_id}` throws. So a string the pattern refuses at parse is exactly the set the engine would resolve or throw on. True.
- `packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts#RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES` is 80, and `boundedOutline` also stops at the body's character bound. "An outline cut by either bound says so" is true.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1. No changeset, the PR carries `skip-changeset`, and an ADR amendment publishes no package. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

The out-of-scope findings of the dev report still stand and predate this diff. Card #37203 now trails the record in four places: it spells the direction `direction`, says "served schema hides", and does not carry the bare value or the placeholder refusal. The seat updates the card; the record governs.

SQL push-down: unchanged. The child read is still one query.

S1: closed. D3 and the header now say "cannot query on", defined as a field outside `getQueryableFields`. The five cases listed are the ones `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms` folds in. The text says the service judges the entry before it reads, so the guard's 403 is never reached, and it keeps "a masked field listed in `fields` is still carried as served". The fallback for a deployment with no answer is the contract's own.

S2: closed. A bare value is read as `$eq`. A whole `{…}` comparand or list member is refused at parse, beside the `$now` anchor, on the platform's own pattern. The author-defect paragraph lists the refusal, and call-time placeholders are in "Later work". The comparand side is now closed: a literal, never a reference.

S3: closed. The header says the maintainer's word names filter and order and no more, and names each addition by point number. "Points that go past the card's words" gains points 13 to 22 with their own introduction, which quotes the word, says what the card adds, and says none is the maintainer's own decision. Point 11 carries the second amendment. `limit` itself is point 13.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Each of points 13 to 22 was read against the tree and the card:

- 13: the card does add a per-list limit, and `RelatedListRequest` takes one. True.
- 14: `get_record` refuses an over-cap `limit` with `.max`. True. Its last sentence is the first nit below.
- 15: the ten operators and the seven left out match `FILTER_OPERATORS`, `LOGICAL_OPERATORS` and the filter form. True.

- 17: matches the resolver, as above. True.
- 18: `SortNodeSchema` is `{ field, order }` and refuses `direction` by alias. True.

- 20: consistent with D1 and D3.
- 21: consistent with D3.

The read set is still unchanged: the delta adds no reference form, and a refused placeholder reads nothing.

Nits, none of which changes the contract:

- Nit: "a door whose own page cap is lower … cuts the list at that cap" is a declaration, not a reading of the tree. On `main` the service's door contract (`door.ts`) has no page cap, and the service reads its cap plus one row whatever the MCP tools' `maxQueryLimit` is. The page cap lives in the tool handlers, not in the bridge. Row 11 either gives the door that member or the sentence never applies. The record should say "row 11" there, as it does for the cap's number.
- Nit: "a string that only contains braces is a literal" reads as a string made of braces. The platform's phrase is a value that merely contains braces.
- Nit: the link-field sentence beside the new rule still says "that caller's schema hides". It is now narrower than the rule next to it. Carried from round 1; a follow-up card should take it.

### Accepted deviations (L2 nits; each takes a prose fix on this PR before hand-over, or a follow-up card)
